advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide/handle whether an explicit `--caused-by` naming an already-linked (derived) culprit should upgrade the stored provenance to `explicit` in `_apply_caused_by`.
evidence: src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:239: `if not culprit or culprit == ticket_id or culprit in existing:` then `return`
`_active_caused_by_targets` returns target ids regardless of provenance (transition_close.py:175-181), so a prior `derived` edge to the same culprit lands in `existing`
The provenance write (`provenance = "explicit" if caused_by.strip() else "derived"`, line 250) is only reached after the guard, so the same-target explicit correction never rewrites the edge
advisory.finding: In `_apply_caused_by`, the `culprit in existing` early-return guard fires before any provenance write, so re-closing a bug (after reopen) with an explicit `--caused-by` naming the SAME target already recorded as a blame-`derived` edge does NOT upgrade the stored provenance to `explicit`; the operator's explicit attribution of an already-linked culprit is silently ignored.
scenarios: Bug closed once via blame auto-derivation (edge marked `derived`), reopened, then re-closed with `--caused-by=<same-culprit>` expecting `explicit` — the edge stays `derived`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting an edge written by backfill(write=True) carries provenance='derived'.
evidence: tests/scripts/test_backfill_caused_by.py:118-123 asserts only target_id: `return [d["target_id"] for d in deps ...]` then `assert _caused_by(sc_bug) == [culprit]` — no provenance assertion
tests/unit/test_caused_by_provenance.py docstring lists close and link paths but NOT the backfill script; search of tests for `backfill` + `provenance` shows no overlap
advisory.finding: The backfill script's newly-added `provenance="derived"` marking is not asserted by any test. scripts/backfill_caused_by.py now writes `_write_link_event(bug_id, culprit_id, "caused_by", tracker_dir, provenance="derived")`, but the existing e2e test (tests/scripts/test_backfill_caused_by.py::test_end_to_end_exactly_one_link_from_two_bugs) asserts only `_caused_by(sc_bug) == [culprit]` (target ids) and `n == 1` — never the provenance value. A regression dropping or mislabeling the backfill provenance (e.g. reverting to no marker, so backfilled guesses read as 'unknown', or setting 'explicit', so guesses read as proven) would pass every test.
scenarios: A refactor of backfill() that drops the provenance kwarg, or a typo setting 'explicit', silently makes backfilled blame-guesses read as proven/unknown in the escape-rate lens
advisory.suggested_fix: In tests/scripts/test_backfill_caused_by.py::test_end_to_end_exactly_one_link_from_two_bugs, extend the caused_by helper to return the dep dict and assert the single-culprit edge has provenance == 'derived'.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm whether the scripts/backfill_caused_by.py provenance edit is authorized, given the file is not in ticket 6536-367c's enumerated Scope/file_impact.
evidence: scripts/backfill_caused_by.py:68-70 comment: `These proposals come from blame auto-derivation, so mark the edge "derived" (ticket 6536-367c)`

Ticket 6536-367c Scope enumerates: _links.py, transition_close.py, _processors.py, common.schema.json, bug_trends.py, docs/event-schema.md, docs/user-guide.md, and the two test files — scripts/backfill_caused_by.py is NOT among them (it is only a plan-review read-path).
advisory.finding: scripts/backfill_caused_by.py is modified to pass provenance="derived" to _write_link_event, but this file is not in the ticket's enumerated Scope/file_impact list (it appears only as a read-path in the plan-review manifest). The diff touches a file beyond the authorized scope.
advisory.suggested_fix: If the backfill-marking behavior is desired, add scripts/backfill_caused_by.py to the ticket's file_impact/Scope (it is a legitimate producer of derived edges, per the event-schema doc) so the change is explicitly authorized rather than a drive-by.
